sentences.text: 1 the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No.
25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 14 namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2636 Bighas 18 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are recorded owner/ cobhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no.
4/20 (416), 21(416), 5/16 (410), 19/6 (416), 7 (416), 8 (114), 14/1 (016), 23/10/2 (105), 11 (313), 19/2 (205) having share as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village K. S. Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.
It is stated that the petitioners are the bhumidhar/absolute owner and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 of the Act was issued.
The said land is free from all encumbrances and no LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 14 litigation in respect of the said land
is pending before any court of law, and was being used for agricultural purposes and having many trees which have not been considered while granting compensation.

6. It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.
The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation.

7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market Dharamvir (2505-06) vs Union Of India (Kirari Suleman Nagar) on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174807251/
2 value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

entities.text: Dharamvir (2505-06) vs Union Of India (Kirari Suleman Nagar)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.

The market value of the acquired land is only to be LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 14 determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 06.02.2006, however,
physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment,
therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.
(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.
No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.

Potentiality means such used to which LAC no.
463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 14 the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards, therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value,
which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after afixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 14 Dharamvir (2505-06) vs Union Of India (Kirari Suleman Nagar) on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174807251/

sentences.text: (vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 23 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Mubarakpur Dabas and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.
The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))

Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 14 market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities, hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH8
, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award.

(ix) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the land in adjoining villages and has also ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by the said land.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - Rs. 5000 per square metre, however,
the land of the petitioner has been valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.
It is and infringement of right of property as laid down in Article 300, that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

(x) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square along with 30% solatium and interest @ 24% with effect from the date of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners are also claiming value of the trees admitted Rs. 1000 per quintal and compensation for the standing crops @ Rs. 1 lakh, compensation of LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir
Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 14 tubewell @ Rs. 5 lakhs and the value of the room @ Rs. 2 lakhs per room alongwith other statutory benefits.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted the said land was acquired for the purpose of PDD, therefore, DDA is a necessary and proper party for complete adjudication of the present reference petition.
The present reference petition U/s 18 of LA Act is time barred therefore, the reference is dismissed on the point of limitation.
Further, the land in question is not surrounded by any developed or underdeveloped colony and can only be used for agriculture.

There were no structures, trees, well or tube well on the Dharamvir (2505-06) vs Union Of India (Kirari Suleman Nagar) on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174807251/

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))

10.

It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

11. It is submitted that the possession of the said land was transferred from L&B/ LAC to DDA on 13.10.2006 whereas, the possession of the land bearing Khasra no. 19//6 (416), 7 (416), 8 (114),
14/1 (016), 23//10/2 (1 05), 11 (313), 19/2 (205) has not been taken by DDA.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 14 factors relevant for determining the compensation
, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.
12.
On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 10.12.2013:  ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to the enhancement in compensation, if so, to what extent?
2. Relief.

sentences.text: Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 459 of 2016, Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India.

entities.text: Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for petitioner and UOI.
None had appeared on behalf of DDA to address the final arguments.
DDA have even failed to file written submissions, though opportunity was granted.
LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14
Therefore, this Court deems it fit to pass judgment on merits of the case.

My issuewise findings and determination are as under : 
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to the enhancement in compensation, if so, to what extent?
15. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled preposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP v. Ram Kumari Devi (1996) 8 SCC 577 as well as in State of UP and Anr.

entities.text: State of UP v. Ram Kumari Devi (1996) 8 SCC 577
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Vs. Rajender Singh AIR 1996 SC 1564:

"The onus is on the petitioner to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
16.
To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Ajit Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 18.10.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
17. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs. Union of India Page no. 12 of 14 18.

Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

sentences.text:
In the case of Ajit Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 25 of 200506 dated 06.02.2006 as Rs.
19,45,800/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.

ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF LAC no. 463/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Dharamvir Vs.
Union of India Page no. 13 of 14 21.

As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No. 19//6 (416), 7 (416), 8 (114), 19//14/1 (016), 23//10/2 (105), 11 (313), 19/2 (205), has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.

22. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT ON 18th DAY OF DECEMBER, 2023.
